sub_agendas_items.title: Motion - Councillor J. Leiper - Potential for CCOC affordable housing development at 261A Hinchey Avenue

motions.motion_text:
WHEREAS the property at 261A Hinchey Avenue is an untraveled former City of Ottawa road allowance; and
WHEREAS The City has been intending to develop the site for affordable housing since 2019, and had previously engaged in conversations with potential proponents to gauge possible interest in the site; and
WHEREAS Council approved the surplus declaration of the site on June 12, 2019, for affordable housing development; the report stated that a housing provider would be selected through a competitive Request for Proposals (RFP); and
WHEREAS to further support future affordable housing development, a Road closure Delegated Authority Report (DAR) was approved on February 6, 2019, and revised on September 6, 2024; and through this process the City committed to maintaining the existing legal access to rear yard parking for the adjacent land-owners at 261 and 263 Hinchey Avenue, and to require any future site owner of 261A Hinchey Avenue to “explore all feasible options to continue to maintain existing access”; and
WHEREAS As part of the Municipal Land Strategy, the site was rezoned to maximize housing potential, and have undertaken a range of due diligence on the site to address property constraints and development requirements; and
WHEREAS On April 16, 2025, Council again approved the transfer of the site to a not-for-profit housing provider to be selected through an RFP process. Through this report, Council also approved the waiver of Section 1.2 of the City’s Disposal of Real Property Policy pertaining to the disposal of real property at current market value, Section 2.3 pertaining to the public marketing of viable properties, and part of Section 4.1 pertaining to the requirement for two appraisals for 261A Hinchey Avenue; and
WHEREAS Centretown Citizens Ottawa Corporation (CCOC) owns the property immediately to the rear of 261A Hinchey Avenue, at 212-216 Carruthers Avenue, and is an experienced builder and operator of affordable housing; and
WHEREAS potential efficiencies may be realized should CCOC have the opportunity to develop and operate a new development at 261A Hinchey Avenue given the proximity of the subject site to CCOC’s other property; and
WHEREAS CCOC has indicated interest in developing new affordable housing at 261A Hinchey Avenue if Section 37 funding were to be made available; and
WHEREAS Approximately 1.3 million dollars are available for affordable housing capital projects through the Ward 15 Section 37 Affordable Housing account, and Councillor Leiper has expressed the intention to direct these funds towards affordable housing development by CCOC at 261A Hinchey Avenue; and
WHEREAS a waiver motion would allow the proponent to save 4-6 months on the process of attaining housing, allowing affordable housing to be brought to market in an accelerated manner.
THEREFORE BE IT RESOLVED that City Council approve the sale of 261A Hinchey Avenue to CCOC and direct staff to negotiate an Agreement of Purchase and Sale to enable the transfer of the subject site to CCOC for a nominal fee; and
BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED that City Council delegate authority to the Director, Housing Solutions, Real Estate and Investment Services, to enter into, conclude, execute, amend, and implement the Agreement of Purchase and Sale with CCOC; and
BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED that Housing Solutions, Real Estate, and Investment Services staff will work with CCOC as the project concept is further designed to ensure project financial feasibility; and
BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED that Staff must be satisfied that the project is financially viable prior to completing the property transfer; and
BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED that level, depth and duration of affordability will be consistent with the City’s Action Ottawa Guidelines. Affordability terms and the required timeline to develop on the subject site will be secured through a future Contribution Agreement between the City and CCOC, covering the land value contribution and provision of Section 37 funds.

sub_agendas_items.title: Motion - Councillor D. Brown - Disposal of Miller’s Oven

motions.motion_text:
WHEREAS Miller’s Oven has been a valued community gathering place for many decades;
WHEREAS Miller’s Oven provides opportunities for members of the community to meet in a low-cost or no-cost facility; and
WHEREAS Miller’s Oven is operated by a volunteer board of directors and is a registered not-for-profit organization; and
WHEREAS Miller’s Oven was originally purchased by the former Rideau Township using funds raised through private donations; and
WHEREAS Finance and Corporate Services Committee (FCSC) recommended Council approve the disposal of 1137 Mill Street at the meeting of February 4th, 2025 under report ACS2025-SI-HSI-0003.
THEREFORE BE IT RESOLVED THAT Finance and Corporate Services Committee recommend Council approve that Miller’s Oven be transferred to the Miller’s Oven Board of Directors for a nominal fee of one dollar; and
BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED THAT staff be directed to execute the transfer of ownership to be effective January 1, 2026;
BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED THAT the City of Ottawa cover any legal or processing fees incurred by this transaction.
